newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah strengthens, swaps lower.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah strengthens, swaps lower.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah strengthened against the dollar and swap rates declined in early trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah continued to recover as regional spillovers eased in the morning.
"The rupiah is on the way to stabilisation and is looking for a new equilibrium level after a band widening and regional corrections," the dealer said.
The central bank widened its the dollar-rupiah band to 12 percent from eight percent following recent de facto devaluations of the Philippine peso and the Thai baht.
One Japanese bank dealer said there was a kind of fight in the morning between onshore and offshore operators, with local players seen consistently countered offshore buying.
"There is some confidence on the local side that there is nothing wrong with the economy," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,446.0/48.0 at 0350 GMT, down from 2,450/55 at the opening. Tomorrow and today rupiah were quoted at 2,445.5/47.0 and 2,445.0/46.5, respectively.
However, dealers said the market remained edgy because of regional factors. "You can't feel well until everything is settled throughout the region," one said.
"It's not so much about Indonesia any more. It's about the region. If speculators eye the peso or the ringgit or the baht again, then we start feeling the jitters," the dealer said.

The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates declined after central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono told Reuters Financial Television in Tokyo that there was room for lower interest rates if inflation continued to slide.
He said operators were seen unloading swaps in response to the comment, but further declines were limited.
"Local operators generally were shorting swaps when offshore came in. Further declines are just good for them to cover, thus slowing a correction in the forward market," the dealer said.
Dealers said swaps were also lower on the back of sustained stable liquidity supply in the money market.
Overnight money fell to 11.0 percent from 15.0 percent. Overnight swap was at 0.38/0.40 and tom/next at 0.65/0.65.
One-month swap was at 16.0/20.0, two down to 30/35 from 33, three to 50.0/55.0 from 70 and six to 102 from 110 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,375/2,679 and the conversion band to 2,433/2,481 on Monday.
